findings.problem: JobWorkflow uses no typestate enum for lifecycle; status is a free-form String and two independent booleans (is_validated, is_sent) allow impossible combinations like status="sent" with is_validated=false.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct JobWorkflow instances with contradictory lifecycle state (e.g., not validated but sent, or status='new' with is_sent=true), violating make-illegal-states-unrepresentable.
findings.fix: Define a JobStatus enum (e.g., Pending, Validated, Sent) with no transitions from invalid to valid states. Remove is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms fields. Encode lifecycle in the enum variants.

findings.problem: status field is pub String, allowing any arbitrary string value (e.g., "SENT", "sent!", "", null-equivalent empty). This breaks any pattern match on state and hides invalid states.
findings.failure_mode: A caller sets status to an unexpected string; downstream logic silently misbehaves or panics when it does not recognize the value, because string equality is the only invariant.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with a domain enum JobStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent }. All transitions go through the enum; no string parsing in the core.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent booleans that do not form a typestate. They can be in inconsistent combinations (validated but not sent, sent but not validated, neither, both without status enum to reconcile).
findings.failure_mode: Logic branching on is_sent without checking status string produces wrong decisions when booleans contradict the status field. No single source of truth for lifecycle.
findings.fix: Collapse is_validated and is_sent into a single JobStatus enum with ordered variants. Transitions become compile-time enforced; no separate booleans needed.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is detached from the lifecycle booleans. sent_at_epoch_ms can be Some(0) while is_sent=false, or None while is_sent=true. The Option is optional lifecycle data that belongs in the variant that owns it.
findings.failure_mode: A sent job has Option::None for sent_at_epoch_ms (lost timestamp) but is_sent=true, or a non-sent job has Some(timestamp) (stale/leaked data). Downstream code cannot trust the optional field independently of lifecycle state.
findings.fix: Move timestamp into the enum variant: enum JobStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }. The timestamp exists only when the job is in the Sent state.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive used as a domain identifier. It carries no rules about format, length, uniqueness, or lifecycle. Any string (empty, whitespace, null-bytes) is accepted.
findings.failure_mode: Empty string id or duplicate ids silently accepted; downstream lookups collide or produce empty-key behavior. No compile-time guarantee that id is a valid identifier.
findings.fix: Introduce a JobId newtype: pub struct JobId(String) or pub struct JobId(u64). Provide a smart constructor that validates format/length and returns a typed error. Use JobId everywhere in the domain.

findings.problem: No smart constructor or parse function exists for JobWorkflow. Raw primitives (String id, String status, bools, Option<u64>) cross the parse boundary without validation. Callers can construct invalid domain states directly via struct literal.
findings.failure_mode: External callers bypass all validation by writing JobWorkflow { id: "".to_string(), status: "".to_string(), is_validated: false, is_sent: false, sent_at_epoch_ms: None } — an entirely invalid state with no error path, no parsing, and no domain enforcement.
findings.fix: Add a private JobWorkflow inner struct and a public constructor: impl JobWorkflow { fn try_new(id: &str, initial_status: &str) -> Result<Self, JobError>. Make all fields private. All mutations go through typed methods that enforce the state machine.

findings.problem: mark_sent unconditionally sets status to "sent" and is_sent to true without checking preconditions. There is no state machine validation (e.g., must be Validated before Sent). Any job, even invalid ones, can be marked sent.
findings.failure_mode: An invalid job (is_validated=false, status="new") can be marked sent in a single function call, with no validation, no error return, and no typestate guard. The function is a fire-and-forget mutation with zero safety.
findings.fix: Replace mark_sent with a fallible method on the typestate enum: fn try_transition_to_sent(self) -> Result<Self, TransitionError>. The method checks that the current state permits the transition and returns a typed error otherwise.

findings.problem: All fields of JobWorkflow are pub. Any caller can mutate status, is_validated, is_sent, sent_at_epoch_ms, or id in place without any validation or state machine enforcement.
findings.failure_mode: A downstream module writes item.status = "deleted" directly, creating an untracked state that mark_sent and all other lifecycle functions do not know about. The structural invariant is entirelyunenforceable from outside the defining module.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide a constructor and state-transition methods. The type itself becomes the guardian of its invariants; no external mutation is possible.

residual_risk: Static review only — no commands run. The crate has pervasive violations of Holzman absolute laws: no typestate enum, no smart constructors, no parse boundary, all-public fields with raw primitives, and unconditional mutation in mark_sent. These are BLOCKER-level defects that make illegal states fully representable. Delivery is blocked until the typestate enum, private fields, typed constructor, and fallible state transitions are implemented.
